newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland needs $1.4 bln to repair flood damage.
newsitem.headline: Poland needs $1.4 bln to repair flood damage.

text.p: Poland will need about 4.8 billion zlotys ($1.4 billion) to repair environmental damage caused by July's catastrophic flooding and mend flood defences, the Environmental Protection Ministry said on Thursday.

A statement said the sum, to be spent up to the year 2010, would be needed to repair retention reservoirs and dams, return rivers to their beds, mend sewage systems, detoxicate soil poisoned by damaged sewage plants and chemical waste dumps, and for other expenses.
Forest damage alone amounts to 240 million zlotys, PAP quoted State Forest Agency head Janusz Dawidziuk as saying.

Total damage remains unknown, but some independent analysts have estimated it at up to 7.5 billion zlotys. The Central Statistical Office (GUS) says the first tentative estimates will be possible in mid-August.

Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki said on Thursday that about 200 million zlotys would be needed make roads and railways usable. Much more will be needed to fully repair the road and rail system and rebuild bridges, he said.
Liberadzki told a news conference that out of more than 3,000 km (1,850 miles) of roads affected by the floods, 1,230 km (750 miles) remained impassable.
The southwestern province of Legnica, one of more than a dozen areas hit by the flood, estimated its damage at 203 million zlotys. Other provinces have not given estimates.
The Agriculture Ministry has estimated that grain losses may amount to 600,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
Analysts estimate Poland's 1997 grain output at between 23.6 and 24.7 million tonnes. In 1996, production was 24.7 million tonnes.
The floods, which hit southwestern Poland nearly four weeks ago, killed 54 people and swamped huge areas of countryside and several big cities.
